newsitem.title: JAPAN: No need for Japan budget for economy - govt sources.
newsitem.headline: No need for Japan budget for economy - govt sources.

text.p: Japan does not need to draft an extra budget to stimulate the economy this fiscal year, senior government officials told Reuters on Friday.

They said the economy was moving in the direction of a recovery led by private-sector demand, with the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) hitting a steady 3.1 percent growth in January-June period from the previous half-year period.
"There is no need to change our view that the economy is recovering gradually. Private demand is taking over from public demand (as the engine of growth)," a ministry official said.
"There is no need for an extra budget for the sake of the economy."

A government official in charge of economic policy also said that the good GDP figures issued earlier on Friday would weaken calls for the government to draft a supplementary budget to finance additional government spending.
The government official added that, even without any supplementary budget later this year, the economy looked very unlikely to start declining.
